chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from one of them, peace be upon them, who said:

"If you perform ghusl after the rising of dawn, that ghusl suffices for janabah, Jumuʿah, ʿArafah, Naḥr, slaughtering, and ziyārah. So when duties owed to Allah come together upon you, a single ghusl suffices for them on your behalf."
He said: Then he said, "Likewise, for the woman, a single ghusl suffices for her janabah, her iḥrām, her Jumuʿah, her ghusl from her menstruation, and her ʿĪd."

And the report narrated by Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying:
"There is no ghusl upon the woman in nifās during travel."

What is meant is only that ghusl is not upon her when she is unable to use water, either because of scarcity of water, fear of cold, or her need for it for drinking; it was not meant that no ghusl is upon her in every circumstance.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهَا: her state of consecration for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, a circumstance affecting the practical ruling here
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءِ: a woman in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: the Friday occasion for which ghusl is recommended or prescribed in context
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, whose availability and use determine applicability of ghusl
key_terms.حَيْضِهَا: her menstruation, after which ritual purification is required
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath performed for purification or devotional occasions

ai.seo_question: Can one ghusl suffice for multiple obligations such as janabah, Jumuʿah, and other ritual occasions?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when multiple causes for ghusl coincide, one ghusl can suffice for all of them. It also clarifies a report about the woman in nifās during travel, explaining that the exemption applies only when using water is not possible or would cause hardship.
